2 علّك القِرْبَةَ , (K,) inf. n. تَعْلِيكٌ, (O, K,) He tanned well the water-skin: (O, K:) mentioned by AHn (TA) and Ibn-'Abbád (O, TA) and Z. (TA.) ―
-b2- علّك مَالَهُ He tended, or managed, well, his cattle, or property. (O, K, TA.) ―
-b3- And علّك يَدَيْهِ عَلَى مَالِهِ He tightened his hands upon his property, from niggardliness, (K, TA,) not entertaining a guest nor giving to a petitioner or beggar. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
